memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Aaron has finished making atonement for the Most Holy Place, the tent of meeting and the altar, he shall bring forward the live goat. He is to lay both hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the wickedness and rebellion of the Israelites — all their sins — and put them on the goat's head. He shall send the goat away into the wilderness in the care of someone appointed for the task." - Lev 16:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Both hands. Pressed down on the goat's head. And out loud, in front of everyone, Aaron confesses the sins of the entire nation.

The gesture matters. Laying hands on the animal was a transfer — this belongs to you now. Everything Israel had done that year, spoken aloud and placed on a living creature.

Notice how thorough the language is: all the wickedness and rebellion... all their sins. Three words, and twice the word all. Nothing was held back. Nothing was considered too shameful to name.

Confession works the same way. Not vague admissions that we are "not perfect," but honest naming of what we have actually done. If we claim to be without sin, we deceive ourselves. But if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us (1 John 1:8-9).

The confession did not cause the atonement — the blood did that. But it was the moment when sin was named and handed over.

And then the goat walks away, carrying what it never did. Surely he took up our pain and bore our suffering (Isa 53:4). The LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all (Isa 53:6).

Christ's head bore what your hands placed there.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are your confessions honest and specific, or vague?
2. What have you never named before God because it feels too shameful?
3. What does it mean that Christ carried what He never did?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I stop being vague. I name before You what I have actually done, and I thank You that Christ carried it away. Thank You for bearing what was never Yours. Amen.
